reported_context.global_effort_interpretation: The athlete did not experience the session as tough overall; aggression was concentrated in quality runs two and three.
reported_context.opening_gate: Green; mind and body clear at 9/10.

route_and_laps.lap_2: Full 2K run one at 75 percent, focusing on corner exit, accurate braking, line choice and body position.
route_and_laps.lap_4: Full 2K run two at 80 percent, adding pedaling on corner exit.
route_and_laps.lap_5: Third climb, RPE 3; athlete reported fatigue 3/10 without assigning it specifically to braking, upper body or legs.
route_and_laps.lap_6: Full 2K run three at 85 percent, with some corner-exit pedaling but relatively more pedaling on flatter trail sections.
route_and_laps.laps_7_to_9: Lap 7 was the required climb to lap 8, lap 8 was Half DH Line as the familiar egress, and lap 9 was the car-park warm-down.

fueling_totals.contents: 1 L 100Plus Active, 20 g honey and 3 g table salt
fueling_totals.calculation_basis: Preserved athlete product values: 48 g carbohydrate and 430 mg sodium per litre of 100Plus Active; a 15 g honey serving supplies 11.3 g carbohydrate and 4.4 mg sodium. Table salt is estimated as 39.34 percent sodium by mass.

session_contract_review.bike_and_setup: Garmin Gear confirms Stumpjumper Expert MY25; athlete explicitly confirms no setup changes.
session_contract_review.trail_condition_and_weather: Very dry trail with some sandy sections.
session_contract_review.fatigue_scope: Overall fatigue was 3/10 before run three; final braking fatigue was 0/10 and upper-body fatigue was 2/10.
session_contract_review.leg_feel_and_any_late_fade: Overall fatigue was explicitly 3/10 before run three, climb RPE fell from 4 to 4 to 3, and no late skill fade occurred. Leg symmetry was not separately rated, so this supports adequate whole-session leg function but not a side-to-side symmetry claim.
session_contract_review.vision_and_decision_speed_first_vs_final: Run one 8/10; run three 9/10 and better organized at the higher intended speed.
session_contract_review.brake_release_and_exit_commitment_first_: Run one prioritized accurate entry braking and corner exit. Run three used deliberate feature-entry braking and speed control, power on exit, and cruising between features; execution was more accurate and aggressive without becoming a speed chase.
session_contract_review.front_tracking_and_dynamic_centre: Front tracking was clean on both runs. The rear was slightly loose on run one, attributed by the athlete probably to body position; it did not recur as an incident on run three.
session_contract_review.pedaling_progression: Run one prioritized corner-exit accuracy. Run two used less appropriate sprint-and-rest timing and carried the highest HR intensity. Run three used more selective exit power and flatter-section pedaling, with deliberate recovery between features.
session_contract_review.technical_quality_notes: Opening gate passed with 9/10 clarity. All three full 2K runs matched the written 75/80/85 percent progression. Run three improved vision and decision speed from 8/10 to 9/10, retained clean front tracking, used accurate entry braking and deliberate exit power, and had no missed line, reactive braking, deflection, rescue, near miss or suspension/chassis fault. Braking fatigue was 0/10 and upper-body fatigue 2/10.

coach_contract_audit.action_alignment_notes: One MTB activity, the correct unchanged Stumpjumper setup, 82.4 minutes inside the 65-90 minute window, three full 2K descents at 75/80/85 percent, climb gates of 4/4/3, and only the required Half-DH-Line egress match the written action. Rider-only technical evidence confirms the final run improved vision/decision speed, retained clean tracking and braking, and produced no rescue event or chassis fault.
coach_contract_audit.load_alignment: Garmin load 200.1 versus the immutable pre-session generic estimate 82.5 and range 57.7-111.4; actual was 142.5 percent above the point estimate and 79.6 percent above the upper bound.
coach_contract_audit.physiology_interpretation: The load is credible rather than a heart-rate artifact: standard Garmin metadata confirms an external ANT+ heart-rate sensor with GOOD battery, ANT+ power was present, average/max HR were 146/184, aerobic/anaerobic Training Effect was 3.7/3.1, TSS was 61.2 and 14.8 minutes accumulated in HR zones 4-5. The session was subjectively manageable and technically bounded while still physiologically meaningful.
coach_contract_audit.predictive_recalibration: The generic duration-by-skill MTB estimate is rejected for this action. Future comparable Stumpjumper three-full-2K prescriptions may use a provisional matched-route-repeat expectation of approximately 196 Garmin load with a conservative 160-220 range, supported by the 2026-07-09 load-191.0 and 2026-08-13 load-200.1 same-bike, external-HR, three-2K actions. This is not an exact full-session match and does not rewrite the frozen 2026-08-13 pre-session prediction.
coach_contract_audit.calibration_disposition: Technical and action review are now clean and complete enough for coaching interpretation, while next-morning response remains pending. The original nominal prescription can never become a matched-load digital-twin calibration row because the immutable generic load estimate missed materially; the delivered route-repeat load remains valid evidence for the separate provisional matched-action prior.

nutrition_interpretation.carbohydrate: 45.9 g/h, inside the written 45-60 g/h execution target and at the lower edge of the generic 45-75 g/h planned-duration profile; adequate for this elapsed duration.
nutrition_interpretation.fluid: 728 mL/h, inside the canonical 500-900 mL/h target. Garmin estimated 754 mL water loss; this is modeled rather than measured.
nutrition_interpretation.sodium: 1176 mg/h, above both today's 600-900 mg/h working target and the canonical 600-1000 mg/h band. If symptom-free it is tolerated evidence, not proof that 3 g added salt is optimal for an 82-minute ride. A future similar one-litre mix would normally use approximately 1.5-2.0 g added table salt unless measured sweat evidence supports more.
